sentences.text: The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Venkateswarlu Nimmagadda

Writ Petition No. 4518 Of 2019
1.

The present writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the constitution
of India seeking the following relief:
 "...to issue an order or direction or writ, more particularly one in the
 nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondent
authorities
a) in not declaring the petitioners' villages of Kudumulur, Besthapalli and Arundhathiwada as
Project Affected Zone.

b) in not initiating acquisition, rehabilitation and resettlement proceedings for acquiring the
properties of the petitioners situated in Kudumulur Besthapalli and its Arundhathiwada by treating
it as project affected zone as highly arbitrary, illegal, null and void against norms of public policy,
violative of fundamental rights guaranteed apart from Article 300-A of the Constitution of India and
consequently to direct the respondent authorities to declare the petitioners' village as Project
Affected Zone and to acquire the same under the Provisions of Right to Fair Compensation
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 and to pass ..."
2. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that, the State of Andhra Pradesh started constructing
Somasila Project on River Penna.

Several villages in Kadapa district were displaced by the foreshore
submersion under the said project.

Kudumulur, Besthapalli & Arundhatiwada are also such villages
affected by the project.

The entire Kudumulur village excluding Bestapalli and Arundhatiwada was
acquired by the government and paid compensation to the lands and structures existed in the said
village.

Nv,J Bestapalli and its Harijanawada of Kudumulur Village were left over from the acquisition
process as they are lying above the contour levels of the project.

3. Learned counsel for petitioner further submits that Kudumuluru, Besthapalli and Arundhatiwada
contains 125 families with a population of more than 600 are residing in the said village.

In view of
the acquisition of Kudumuluru Village and its hamlets leaving part of Kudumuluru village i.e.
Besthapalli and Arundhathwada as left over.

Now the Somasila Project is completely impounded
with its optimum level of storage.

In view of the Impounding of the project, the backwaters are
stagnated on all the sides of Besthapalli and Arundhatiwada due to which the connection to the
outer world severed and there is no way to reach the said villages.

4.

It is submitted that Besthapalli and Arundhatiwada villages are surrounded by the river Penna of
East and Northern sides, South and Western sides are surrounded by "Sri Penusila Lakshmi
Narasimha Swamy Abhayaranyam" which includes a hillock on southern side and plain land on the
western sides.

Once the back water stagnates and reaches the optimum level of project, the village
will be surrounded by water on three sides and hillock will prevent the villages from reaching to the
outer world and there will be completely communication cut off to the village for months together
till the water level in the project is recedes.

During the said period the Nv,J poisonous creatures and
wild animals enter into the village and cause harm to the human life.

It is even very difficult to
approach to hospital due to ill health or untoward incident in the hands of the wild animals or
poisonous snakes.

As there would not be any way to go out of the village except crossing the hillock,
which practically impossible as the same is covered with dense forest of "Sri Penusila Lakshmi
Narasimha Swamy Abhayaranyam".
5.

It is further submitted that in view of the acquisition of entire lands and other properties of all the
hamlets of Kudumuluru Revenue village and surrounding villages within the mandal, the petitioners
are deprived of their livelihood as petitioners have no agricultural land and no other agricultural
works in the area.

Apart from the above, as stated above, in view of the inundation of the land on all
the three sides and obstruction due to hill and thick forest on the other side, petitioners have no
source of living in the said village and even no possibility to approach the other villages for coolie
works.

6. The learned counsel for petitioners further submits that, petitioners made a representation to the
Government of Andhra Pradesh requesting to acquire petitioners village and to provide R & R
package to our village apart from paying compensation, as the said village Is a project affected
village.

In spite of repeated requests and persuasion through the authorities as well as Nv,J the
public representatives, the government has not taken any action so far.

Aggrieved by the same, the
present writ petition is filed.

7. It is submitted that, once the project is fully impounded, the village will lose communication from
the rest of the world and all the villagers are left with no work and no source of l

iving and are subjected to starvation in the peninsula and are subjected to various water effect deceases like Malaria and other viral deceases, in view of the stagnation of water and contamination of drinking water in the village and also facing starvation in view of either non-availability of any work or no access to the food, medical facility, transport and other amenities like electricity etc.

In view of the acquisition of the entire surrounding areas and due to inundation of the agricultural lands in surrounding villages, it become very difficult to lead lives by petitioners in the village.

Therefore,
petitioners are the most effected persons in the village under the project and it required to be acquired by the respondent authorities.

In similar situations in neighbouring Mandal in Kadapa District namely Penagalur, two villages i.e. Perlakunta and Merlabylu villages also faced the very same problem under the same project wherein the government has acquired all the properties and the entire villages were rehabilitated vide Award No. 4 of 2013, dated 12.08.2013.
Where as in the instant case the respondent authorities have not taken any steps.
Similarly in respect of Pothapi village.

Nandaluru Mandal was also considered as project affected zone under the same project and process is NV,J initiated for declaring the left over village of Pothapi as project affected zone, vide G Chalapathi vs The State Of Ap on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2446966/
2 memo No. 1919795/R & R A2/2018-1, dated 22.11.2018.

sentences.text: Whereas in the instant case the respondent authorities are neither initiating any proceedings for acquiring petitioners land nor to declare the area as project affected zone.

Therefore, the action of the respondent authorities is highly arbitrary,
illegal, null and void against the norms of public policy and violative fundamental rights apart from Article 300-A of the Constitution of India.

8. Learned Government Pleader for Irrigation filed counter affidavit on behalf of Respondent No.5 - Executive Engineer, Somasila Project Division No.IV, Atmakur, SPSR Nellore Distrcit, wherein it is submitted that the entire Kudumulur village excluding Bestapalli, Arundhathiwada was acquired by the Government under the Somasila Project is factually incorrect and therefore denied.

As per the records, compensation was paid to the villagers of Bestapalli, Arundhathiwada and Harizanawada,
H/o Kudumulur Village in Vontimitta Mandal (hereinafter referred as subject villages) under the Somasila Project on 14.09.1989.

The villagers of Subject villages after receiving the compensation long back under the Somasila Project were migrated to nearby safe location situated at above FRL 330 contour of the Somasila Reservoir and settled themselves by constructing houses in the Government land bearing Survey Nos 173 & 175 of Kudumulur Revenue Village in Vontimitta Mandal.
NV,J 9.

After receiving the notices in the present Writ Petition the Engineering Officials i.e. Executive Engineer, S.P. Division No. IV, Atmakur, Deputy Executive Engineer, LA&R Sub Division and Asst Executive Engineer, LA&R Sub Division, Badvel from the Engineering Department) and Revenue officials(Special Collector(LA), GNSS, Kadapa, Special Deputy Collector(LA), SSP Unit-IV,
Rajampet, Kadapa District and other supporting staff from the Revenue Department) of the Somasila Project have conducted inspection jointly on 04.03.2020 in the newly formed Villages of Bestapalli, Arundhatiwada and Harizanawada in order to know the ground realities.

During the interaction with the villagers of said Bestapalli, Arundhathiwada and Harizanawada, agreed that they have received compensation long back under the Somasila Project and moved to nearby safe location which is not a submerged area under the back water of Somasila Reservoir and started living by constructing houses in the Government land belonging to the Kudumulur revenue village in Vontimitta Mandal.
10. Learned Government Pleader further submitted that during the inspection, it is observed that there are no communication facilities to these newly formed villages.
The road connecting these villages got damaged with pot holes and ditches.

Further during the visit of said villages, the villagers requested the authorities to provide required basic infrastructure to lead their life instead of shifting them from the newly formed villages where they NV,J are currently residing.
Hence the said villages cannot be declared as Project affected Zone.
11. It is further submitted that the compensation was already paid to the villagers of subject villages long back under the Somasila Project.

Hence the compensation cannot be paid once again to the same villagers under the Somasila Project as they have moved voluntarily to the nearby safe location after receiving compensation at their old villages.

Further the location where they are currently G Chalapathi vs The State Of Ap on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2446966/
3 residing is not notified as submerged area under the back waters of Somasila Reservoir since the location is situated at above FRL 330 contour of the Reservoir.

sentences.text: 12. The petitioners have been residing in a location which is above FRL 330 contour height of the reservoir and the said area is not a submerged area.

The petitioners have filed the present Writ Petition seeking acquisition of land by invoking the provision of The Right To Fair Compensation And Transparency In Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation And Resettlement Act, 2013 (henceforth Act 30 of 2013)and the original villagers of subject villages which are hamlets of Kudmuluru Village have already been paid compensation long ago, the Petitioners cannot claim compensation once again for the said purpose.

sentences.text: Since, the area in which petitioners are now residing is not a project affected area, compensation cannot be paid by NV,J invoking the Act 30 of 2013.
Hence the Writ Petition is liable to be dismissed.

13. On the other hand Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition filed counter affidavit on behalf of Respondent Nos. 3, 4, & 6, wherein it is submitted that, Kudumalur village, Vontimitta Mandal, YSR District is one among the submerged villages under the foreshore waters of Somasila Project.

As per the requisition of the Executive Engineer, Irrigation and Project Division, Somasila Project, Division No.IV, Atmakur, the lands in Kudumalur village were divided into 8 reaches for sake of convenience.
Draft Notification and Draft Declaration were published under section 4(1) and 6 of Land Acquisition Act 1894 in the years 1996 and 1997.
Awards were passed vide Award No.9/98-99 dated 16.01.1999 etc., and compensation was paid to the land owners.
Similarly structures were also acquired in Kudumalur village and compensation was paid to the structure owners.
14. It is submitted that, Bestapalli is H/o Kudumalur village.
It is also under foreshore submersion under Somasila Project.

The Executive Engineer, Irrigation and Project Division, Somasila Project,
Division No.1V, Atmakur sent requisition for acquisition of structures in Bestapalli Ho Kudumalur village.

Draft Notification was approved by Government in G.O.Rt.No.2184/1 & P (PR Wing)
Department dated 29.12.1980 and Draft Declaration was approved vide Government Memo No.3896/LAR-I(2) SD-1 NV,J dated 29.12.1980.
It was published in Andhra Pradesh Gazette No.91 dated 26.02.1981.
Award enquiry was conducted in Bestapalli H/o Kudumalur village on 04.09.1986 and 05.09.1986.
No objections were received at the time of the award enquiry.
Award was passed vide No.28/86-87 dated 18.09.1986 to the structures in Reach No.1 of Bestapalli village H/o Kudumalur.
Similarly award was passed vide Award No.29/86-87 dated 18.09.1986 to structures in Reach No.ll of Bestapalli village H/o Kudumalur.
to the structures in Reach No.III of Bestapalli village Ho Kudumalur.
The contention of the petitioners that the entire Kudumalur village excluding Bestapalli, Arundhatiwada was acquired by the Government under the Somasila Project is not correct.

The villagers of subject villages, after receiving compensation long back under the Somasila Project have migrated to a nearby safe location situated at above FRI, 330 contour of the Somasila Reservoir and settled themselves by constructing houses in the Government land bearing Sy.Nos. 173 and 175 of Kudumalur Revenue village of Vontimitta mandal.

It is further submitted that after receiving the notices in the present writ petition, the Special Collector (LA), GNSS, Kadapa, Special Deputy Collector (LA), Somasila Project, Unit-IV, Rajampet,
YSR District along with Executive Engineer, Somasila Project, Division No.IV, Atmakur, Deputy Executive Engineer, LA and R sub-division and Assistant Executive Engineer, LA and R sub-division, Badvel have conducted joint inspection on NV,J 04.03.2020 in the newly formed village of subject villages in order to know the ground realities.

During the interaction with the villagers of the said subject villages, the villagers stated that they have received compensation long back under the Somasila Project and since then shifted to a nearby safe location which is not a submerged area under the back water of Somasila Reservoir.
They stated that they have been residing by constructing houses in Sy No.173, 175 which are un-assessed waste lands pertaining to Kudumalur Revenue village in Vontimitta Mandal.
The villagers have stated that they are eking out a livelihood by fishing in the back waters of Somasila Project which are near their present new village.
They said that the Forest Department Officials are objecting frequently to the fishing activity in the back waters.
Further they stated that there is no proper road facility from their newly settled village to Vontimitta for a stretch of 2 K.M. and there is no drinking water availability in the village
and therefore urged to provide the basic facilities to them in the newly settled village.
16. On inspection of newly formed villages i.e subject villages on 04.03.2020, it is observed that there are insufficient communication facilities in these villages.
The connecting road of these villages is a mud and rocky katcha road, which was badly damaged and replete with pot holes and undulations.

Therefore the villagers have requested the authorities to provide basic infrastructure facilities for a decent living instead of shifting NV,J them from the newly formed villages where they are presently residing.
Hence the said villages cannot be declared as Project Affected Zone.
The compensation was already paid to the villagers of subject villages long back under the Somasila Project.

Hence the compensation cannot be paid once again to the same villagers under the Somasila Project as they have shifted on their volition to the nearby safe location after receiving compensation at their old villages.
Further the location where they are presently residing is not submerged area under the back waters of Somasila Reservoir since the location is situated at above FRL 330 contour of the reservoir.
The villagers have stated in writing that they require infrastructural facilities for a decent living in the newly formed villages of subject villages.
They have not insisted for declaration as Project Affected village as averred in the petition.

17. It is further submitted that the petitioners stated that in similar situation in neighboring mandal in Kadapa District namely, Penagalur, two villages i.e., Perlakunta and Merlabylu villages also faced the very same problem under the same project wherein the Government has acquired all the properties and the entire villages were rehabilitated vide Award No.4 of 2013, dated 12.08.2013 whereas in the instant case, the respondent authorities have not taken any steps.

Similarly in respect of Pothapi village, Nandalurmandal was also considered as Project Affected Zone under the same project and process is initiated for declaring the left over village of Pothapi of Project Affected Zene,
vide memo No.1919795/R & R-A2/2018-1.
NV,J Dated 22.11.2018 whereas in the instant case the respondent authorities are neither initiating any proceedings for acquiring their land nor declared the area as Project Affected Zone.

sentences.text: It is submitted that Perlakunta and Marlbailu villages in Penagalur mandal have become totally inaccessible due to construction of Somasila Project.

All the Government Revenue poramboke lands available around Mallemadugu, Perlakunta and Marlabailu are then surveyed the lands are proposed to be handed over to Forest Department for compensatory afforestation.
These villages have become inaccessible and remained as Islands in the middle of the Forest Lands.

The District Collector, Kadapa has recommended that it would be preferable to acquire the villages and resettle them in Damencherla as it is cost saving and also administratively desirable in view of the breakdown of communication for the villages and requested to accord Government sanction for acquiring these villages under Somasila Project.
Government has issued directions to acquire the lands and structures of Perlakunta and Marlbailu villages of Penagalur mandal, YSR District for social afforestation under Somasila Project.
As per the requisition of the Executive Engineer, SP Division, Somasila, Nellore, 39 structures were acquired for compensatory afforestation vide Award No.4/2013-14 dated 12.08.2013.
NV,J 19.

In case of Pothapi village, Government has issued memo No.1919795/R & R-A2/2018-1 dated 22.11.2018 and declared the entire Pothapi village, Nandalurmandal of YSR Kadapa District as Project Affected Zone.

During 11/2007, due to good inflows and floods in Pennar Catchment, the Somasila Reservoir was impounded up to 70.632 TMC (+326.68) for the first time and hence all the road connectivity leading to Pothapi main village was inundatedand the reservoir back water entered on three sides of the Pothapi village in which communication cutoff with other villages was observed.
Unlike in the Bestapalli, Arundhatiwada and Harijanawada, none of the structures in Pothapi village were acquired and paid compensation earlier.
Hence the case of Perlakunta and Merlabylu villages and Pothapi village are different from the case of Bestapali, Arundhatiwada and Harijanawada.
20. It is submitted that the petitioners have been residing in a location which is above FRL 330 contour of the reservoir and the said area is not a submerged area.

The original villagers of Bestapalli, Arundhatiwada and Harijanawada H/o Kudumalur have already been paid compensation long ago, hence the petitioners cannot claim compensation again for the same purpose.

As the area in which the petitioners now residing is not a project affected area,
compensation cannot be paid as per LARR Act, 2013.
It is liable for dismissal.
NV,J 21.

Learned counsel for petitioner filed rejoinder affidavit wherein it is submitted that, it is not in dispute that the village of Kudumuluru Besthapalli and Harijanawada are land locked and even as per the statements obtained by the respondent authorities dated 04.03.2020 clearly indicate that there is no road facility to reach the village and it is covered by water and hillocks on all the sides.

It is further submitted that the respondent authority under the guise of enquiry for declaring the villages as project effected zone obtained the signature on white papers and got drafted the statement dated 04.03.2020 to suit to their purpose.

The respondent authority obtained the said statement alleged to have been signed by 31 persons was not after appraising the facts of the G Chalapathi vs The State Of Ap on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2446966/
6 statement to the signatories and they were misled by the authorities informing that they are causing the enquiry for the purpose of declaring the village as project affected zone.

sentences.text: Therefore the contention advanced by the respondent authorities that they were paid compensation and these villages are formed from the original habitation after receipt of compensation is absolutely baseless and no material is forthcoming to establish the said fact.

The other contentions made contra are no way relevant to the present issue of declaration of the above said villages as the project affected zone and all the averments are nothing but misinterpretation of facts with a view to mislead this Court to avoid declaration of the villages as the project affected zone.
NV,J 22.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner; learned Government Pleader for Irrigation and learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and perused the material available on record.
23. Undoubtedly, the petitioners hail from the villages of Kudumuluru, Besthapalli, and Arundatiwada, collectively comprising approximately 125 families with a population exceeding 600 residents.
The construction of the Somasilla project by the state of Andhra Pradesh on the River Penna resulted in the displacement of numerous villages in Kadapa district, including subject villages.
Compensation was provided for the lands and structures within our villages, but we were resettled approximately 33 years ago at an elevation of 330 contour level.

24. However, due to the project's impoundment reaching its optimum storage level, stagnant backwaters now encroach upon Besthapalli and Arundathiwada, particularly on their eastern and northern sides where the River Penna flows.
Additionally, the villages are hemmed in by hillocks and the Penusila Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Abhayaranyam to the west and south, effectively isolating us from the outside world.
During periods of inundation, communication with the outside world becomes severely restricted, lasting for months until the water recedes.
NV,J 25.

The petitioners further contend that during these periods, the villages are vulnerable to incursions by poisonous creatures, snakes, and wild animals, posing significant risks in case of medical emergencies or other untoward incidents.
Access to medical facilities requires traversing a 16- kilometer journey across the hillock, exacerbating the challenges faced during emergencies.

26. It is observed that the formation of subject villages happened at the initial stages of Somasila Project and they might have been an impression that this subject place would be the satisfaction, but as of now, due to the improvement of water, the project reached to its optimum level, the safe location of 30 years ago, now it became project affected area.
The contentions raised by the petitioner needs to be addressed by the first respondent herein.

Being a welfare state, it cannot deny the rightful claim of the petitioners on the ground that, earlier they even paid compensation and they themselves voluntarily shifted the present location, for the reason that, naturally the people should have so much passion, love affection, attachment and emotion towards their native location.
That feeling must have driven them to have resettlement at the present location.

Moreover they G Chalapathi vs The State Of Ap on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2446966/
7 would not have visualized the present scenario.

sentences.text: Even according to the report of the Advocate Commissioner, as narrated in the counter affidavit, the petitioners lack minimum amenities to lead minimum dignity of life.
Having NV,J observed the facts as narrated in the report of the Advocate Commissioner, it indicates that the petitioners were deprived of everything.

27. In view of the facts and circumstances, as described in the report of the Advocate Commissioner,
the claim of the petitioners should be considered on par with Mallimadugu, Perlakunta and Marlabailu Villages of Pengaluru Mandal.

Further, having received the compensation in earlier occasion, now they cannot claim anything as contended by the respondents, is contrary to the basic principles of a democratic welfare state and also contrary to Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

28. It is further observed that there is no material placed before this Court to substantiate the contention of the respondents that the petitioners were already paid the compensation under the Award.
But, the same was denied by the petitioners in their rejoinder.
These facts appears that the petitioners were allowed to make structures on their own at the present habitation area, which is a Government poramboke land, in lieu of compensation.

29. The contention of the learned Government Pleader that they themselves voluntarily formulated/established present habitation at Government land in very safe zone and even the petitioners have requested for road connectivity, power and other civil amenities only, but not for acquisition, as canvassed now and 31 of them also submitted written statements out of 141 people,
which was denied by the petitioners by their NV,J reply affidavit.

Even assuming that some of the requested only for providing amenities, but due to disconnection/dis-communication due to improvement at optimum level in the project and so many other factors as narrated, which are indicating that the petitioners cannot lead their lives in normal course and their lives would be in danger, their children would be deprived of everything.
30. During periods of inundation, communication with the outside world becomes severely restricted, lasting for months until the water recedes.
During these periods, the villages are vulnerable to incursions by poisonous creatures, snakes, and wild animals, posing significant risks in case of medical emergencies or other untoward incidents.
Access to medical facilities requires traversing a 16-kilometer journey across the hillock, exacerbating the challenges faced during emergencies.
Despite appeals to recognize the subject villages as project-affected and provide appropriate rehabilitation and resettlement measures, the government has yet to take any action in this regard.
Hence, we seek the intervention of this court to declare our villages as project-affected zones and initiate proceedings for acquisition, rehabilitation, and resettlement.

31. In response to the contentions raised by the respondents, the petitioners submitted a rejoinder,
specifically contesting the alleged statements obtained from villagers under misrepresentation during an NV,J inquiry to declare the village as a Project Affected Zone.
To ascertain the ground reality, this Court appointed an Advocate Commissioner.

32. The Advocate Commissioner visited the villages on 11.11.2023 in the presence of representatives from both petitioners and respondent authorities, as detailed in the report submitted on 23.11.2023.

sentences.text: The report highlights that the villages are located approximately 16 kilometers away from the mandal headquarters, lacking proper road facilities.

It identifies 141 structures within the village,
delineated in Sy.No.175/1 (76 structures), Sy.No.401 (14 structures), and Sy.No. 173/1 (41 Structures) as per the Field Measurement Book (FMB).
The village is bounded by the submerged project area to the east and north, Anumkonda hill to the west, and forest with a katcha rastha to the south.
33. Regarding amenities, neither the government nor the villagers provided a provision for drinking water, with villagers resorting to digging borewells for their needs.
The village consists of self-built elementary school up to 5th standard, which is only public facility.
However, during peak water levels, snakes, rodents, and communicable diseases pose significant threats.
The report notes that the villagers relocated to the current location 33 years ago due to the original village's acquisition.
The katcha road, also constructed by villagers, is impassable during rainy seasons, leading to communication cutoffs and difficulties in accessing medical facilities.
NV,J 34.
The report highlights the village's isolation during project inundation and the absence of basic facilities like health centers.
The state's stance, citing previous compensation and voluntary resettlement, is deemed untenable given the circumstances leading to settlement.
The state must prioritize the welfare of villagers by improving living standards and initiating necessary proceedings for rehabilitation.
It is evident that the village qualifies as a project-affected zone, necessitating appropriate action to address the villagers' plight and facilitate their rehabilitation.

35. Hence, in view of the facts and circumstances of this case, this writ petition is disposed of,
directing Respondent Nos.1 to 6 to consider the petitioners villages as Project Affected Zone, and pass appropriate orders within a period of three (03) months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
No costs.
36. Consequently, miscellaneous applications pending if any, shall stand closed.

In view of the acquisition of the entire surrounding areas and due to inundation of the agricultural lands in surrounding villages, it become very difficult to lead lives by petitioners in the village.
Therefore,
petitioners are the most effected persons in the village under the project and it required to be acquired by the respondent authorities.
The petitioners have filed the present Writ Petition seeking acquisition of land by invoking the provision of The Right To Fair Compensation And Transparency In Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation And Resettlement Act, 2013 (henceforth Act 30 of 2013)and the original villagers of subject villages which are hamlets of Kudmuluru Village have already been paid compensation long ago, the Petitioners cannot claim compensation once again for the said purpose.
Since, the area in which petitioners are now residing is not a project affected area, compensation cannot be paid by NV,J invoking the Act 30 of 2013.
Hence the Writ Petition is liable to be dismissed.
As the area in which the petitioners now residing is not a project affected area,
compensation cannot be paid as per LARR Act, 2013.
The construction of the Somasilla project by the state of Andhra Pradesh on the River Penna resulted in the displacement of numerous villages in Kadapa district, including subject villages.
Additionally, the villages are hemmed in by hillocks and the Penusila Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Abhayaranyam to the west and south, effectively isolating us from the outside world.
During periods of inundation, communication with the outside world becomes severely restricted, lasting for months until the water recedes.
The petitioners further contend that during these periods, the villages are vulnerable to incursions by poisonous creatures, snakes, and wild animals, posing significant risks in case of medical emergencies or other untoward incidents.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further, having received the compensation in earlier occasion, now they cannot claim anything as contended by the respondents, is contrary to the basic principles of a democratic welfare state and also contrary to Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
The state's stance, citing previous compensation and voluntary resettlement, is deemed untenable given the circumstances leading to settlement.
It is evident that the village qualifies as a project-affected zone, necessitating appropriate action to address the villagers' plight and facilitate their rehabilitation.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The state must prioritize the welfare of villagers by improving living standards and initiating necessary proceedings for rehabilitation.
35. Hence, in view of the facts and circumstances of this case, this writ petition is disposed of,
directing Respondent Nos.1 to 6 to consider the petitioners villages as Project Affected Zone, and pass appropriate orders within a period of three (03) months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
No costs.
36. Consequently, miscellaneous applications pending if any, shall stand closed.
